transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marc Diaz (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (AcmeCorp Head of Search), Maya Li (AcmeCorp ML Engineer), Jordan Greene (AcmeCorp Platform Lead)

Summary: Quick hosted-API walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank endpoints and a search relevance workflow. SE demoed end-to-end: embedding generation, vector store integration patterns, Redwood 'rerank' endpoint for cross-encoder reordering, and Console metrics/Optimize suggestions. Questions on scale, latency, data residency, SOC2 and integration with existing Elastic stack. Agreed next steps: send hosted pricing & security pack, share notebook, customer to provide dataset for benchmark and schedule POC check-in.

Topics:
- Embeddings endpoint usage patterns (batching, dims, normalization)
- Rerank API (when to use vs ANN filtering)
- Vector DB integration patterns (hybrid with Elastic/OpenSearch)
- Console observability and Redwood Optimize suggestions
- Security: SOC2, data retention, SSO/SAML, KMS

Action items (brief): see metadata for owners/dates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood, i'll hand over to marc our solutions engineer for the technical walkthrough, quick 40-ish minute demo and then q&a, sound good?
[00:10] Ravi: yeah thanks lena, really excited. we talked a bit in email, main goals are improving search relevance across our product catalog and reducing false positives, we currently use Elastic and some heuristics.
[00:25] Marc: great, thanks ravi. quick agenda: embeddings for semantic recall, then a simple ANN + rerank pattern, and finally console ops and optimize suggestions. i'll show a live notebook and the hosted api calls.
[00:40] Maya: quick note, we're constrained on latency (p95 < 120ms for user search) and cost per q isn't huge but matters. also we have ~15M product docs but for POC we'll start with 1k.
[01:05] Marc: perfect, i'll call out latency tradeoffs. ok jumping in, here's the embeddings endpoint - POST /v1/embeddings, returns 1024-d vectors by default for the model we selected. we do batch embeddings to amortize network and tokenization cost. code snippet: (///) "client.embeddings.create({model:'redwood-embed-1024', input: [..]})"
[01:40] Marc: note: we recommend normalizing vectors client-side if you're using cosine similarity in your vector DB, or you can use dot-product with unnormalized. small transcription note: i said "normal eyes" earlier, meant normalize.
[02:05] Jordan: you mentioned model redwood-embed-1024, is that hosted only? do we get model versions?
[02:18] Marc: yes hosted model catalog, version pinning supported. for dedicated/private deployments customers can bring their own or use on-prem variants. for hosted we'll surface performance profile in console.
[02:45] Marc: next, ANN filtering - you do nearest neighbor recall in your vector DB (we tested with Pinecone/Weaviate and even Elastic vectors), get top N candidates, then call our rerank endpoint to do a cross-encoder style reordering using the full context. rerank call is POST /v1/rerank with parameters: query, candidates[], return_scores:true.
[03:10] Marc: i'll demo: first we embed query, search vector DB, get top 50, then call rerank. rerank uses a heavier model so latency is higher but you only run it over small N. it's a common pattern to keep p95 low while improving final relevance.
[03:35] Maya: what's the typical latency on rerank for N=50? and costs?
[03:40] Marc: on hosted for rerank with model "redwood-rerank-v1" we see median around ~60-120ms per request depending on seq len and concurrency, cost is model-dependent — for demos we show per-request estimates in console. for POC we can benchmark with your 1k dataset, we'll provide a script.
[04:05] Ravi: would we have to move away from Elastic if we want to use rerank?
[04:10] Marc: not at all. hybrid pattern: keep Elastic for filtering/metadata and ANN for vectors or use Elastic's vector capabilities to do ANN, then call rerank. we actually see a lot of customers keep metadata in Elastic and use a separate vector index.
[04:30] Jordan: how does this integrate with our infra? firewall, VPC peering, data residency?
[04:40] Lena: good question — for hosted we have region selection and data handling controls; we offer Private deployments for stricter residency or VPC options. i'll follow up with the security pack — SOC2, ISO docs, SSO/SAML, and KMS notes.
[05:00] Marc: demo time — shared screen: notebook with step 1: embed a batch of 10 queries, push vectors to a toy vectorstore (we used faiss in the notebook), then perform a similarity lookup.
[05:25] [05:30] Marc: note in the transcript the notebook printed some noisy tokens, so apologies if transcription shows weird tokens like "faus" when i said faiss. haha.
[06:00] Marc: here's the emb call response, vector dims 1024, i show cosine scores; then i run a kNN search, get ~top50, then call rerank. code: "client.rerank.create({model:'redwood-rerank-v1', query: q, candidates: candidates})"
[06:30] Marc: rerank returns per-candidate scores and an ordered list, you can store rerank scores or just return top result to user. also we have a fast option for rerank-lite which is cheaper but less accurate for some cases.
[06:55] Maya: does rerank look at documents as full text or only snippets? we often have long descriptions, and product specs can be long.
[07:05] Marc: it works on the candidate text you pass. common pattern: pass a short snippet plus metadata. if you need long context we chunk and pass aggregated representations, or use a semantic highlight step. there are tradeoffs for token costs.
[07:30] Ravi: curious about failure modes — if rerank model hallucinates or boosts wrong docs, how do we monitor?
[07:40] Marc: great point. Console has per-route metrics: token counts, latency, top tokens, and we expose evaluation hooks — you can run labeled queries and compare recall/precision before/after. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching/quantization and flag regressions. we also have logging integration so you can store request/response for auditing (configurable retention).
[08:10] Jordan: retention is configurable? for hosted?
[08:15] Lena: yes, retention and logging controls; default is short retention for hosted but we can agree on SLR terms for enterprise. again we'll include this in the security pack.
[08:35] Marc: switching gears — scaling: we recommend asynchronous batch workers for indexing (embeddings at ingest time) and real-time embedding for queries. for 15M docs you can do offline embed pipeline with autoscaling workers, then store in vector DB. for incremental updates we support bulk endpoints.
[09:05] Marc: here's a note on metrics — cost per query can be reduced by lowering rerank N (e.g., N=10 instead of 50) or using a cheaper emb model for recall and a stronger one only for rerank. Redwood Optimize can recommend those profiles based on your query distribution.
[09:40] Maya: we care about p95 under load — do you have per-tenant SLOs?
[09:45] Lena: for hosted we have published performance profiles; Dedicated gives stronger guarantees and SLAs. We'll scope that if POC looks good.
[09:58] Marc: quick live demo of console — showing route-level dashboards: tokens per call, avg latency, cost breakdown, and a sample rollout where you can canary rerank changes. (i scroll) you'll see an optimize suggestion: "reduce batch size for embedding ingestion to avoid memory spikes" — this is simulated in the demo.
[10:35] Ravi: can we hook our own metrics into that? we have DataDog and internal monitoring.
[10:40] Marc: yes, we have tracing hooks and metrics export to Prometheus/DataDog and webhooks for alerts.
[11:00] Marc: switching back to rerank details — if you want deterministic scoring, we support seeding and stable versioning, and we log model version with each call.
[11:25] Maya: about costs — do you quote per-token or per-request for rerank?
[11:30] Marc: rerank is per-request + token usage; console will show per-route cost. during trial we can map expected qps to cost estimates.
[11:45] Jordan: what's the onboarding like for our platform team? we want minimal infra changes.
[11:50] Lena: typical onboarding: quickstart, sample code, a pilot project (1k docs), bench script. our AE/SE help with initial tuning. For Dedicated or Private we can provide templates for VPC peering and bastion setup — but for hosted most customers integrate with vector DB and existing auth.
[12:10] Marc: demo note: i triggered a sample rerank call, results reordered and i highlight a few examples where semantic match overtook lexical match. you can see the score deltas in the result.
[13:05] Ravi: these look promising — what's the best way to evaluate quality? should we do MRR, NDCG?
[13:10] Marc: we recommend NDCG/MRR and A/B against your current Elastic baseline. we'll give you a benchmark harness; i'll drop a link to the notebook and a small script to compute these metrics.
[13:35] Maya: latency under concurrency — if we do rerank at N=50 and qps 200, does that mean we need extra capacity?
[13:45] Marc: yes you'll need to account for rerank concurrency. common pattern: synchronous rerank for user-facing low qps, asynchronous re-ranking for heavy loads, or reduce N. Dedicated can provide reserved capacity.
[14:05] [14:15] Marc: side note: some words in transcript may be off — the engine picked up "redwood-optimize" as "red would optimist" earlier, so forgive typos.
[14:30] Ravi: security questions — do you support SAML SSO for console? audit logs?
[14:35] Lena: yes SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. we also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private deployments. security pack will include SOC2 report and encryption notes.
[15:00] Maya: do you store PII? we try to avoid sending raw user identifiers, is it possible to mask or hash before sending?
[15:10] Marc: absolutely, common pattern is to hash or pseudonymize PII before sending; we also support a no-logging option for enterprise tiers.
[15:30] Jordan: any rate limits? we'll have bursty indexing at times.
[15:35] Lena: hosted has rate limits and quotas; Dedicated gives more throughput; we can discuss burst agreements in contract.
[15:50] Marc: jumping back to demo, now showing the quickstart in the console — how to create API key, route config, choose model and rerank params, and enable logging.
[16:25] Marc: question from my side — do you currently use any embedding model in prod?
[16:30] Ravi: not in prod, we've toyed with open-source models locally but no standardized flow.
[16:40] Marc: ok good, then the notebook will help kickstart. i'll share an example that integrates with Elastic by storing ids and metadata in Elastic and vectors in a separate vector index.
[17:05] Maya: curious about vector dimension tuning — is 1024 always better?
[17:10] Marc: not always; sometimes 512 dims are fine and cheaper. Redwood Optimize can suggest model/quantization choices based on empirical error/cost tradeoffs.
[17:35] Ravi: how do we validate rerank doesn't introduce bias?
[17:40] Marc: you can run labeled query suites and check for shifts; Console can surface regression alerts and Optimize will flag quality regressions tied to prompt sets/evals.
[18:00] Marc: final demo bit — i show a canary rollout where we toggle rerank model for 10% traffic and measure NDCG delta before full rollout.
[18:25] Jordan: nice. what's support like during POC?
[18:30] Lena: SE support during pilot, weekly check-ins, and a playbook for benchmarks. after POC we can discuss Dedicated if you need SLAs.
[18:50] Ravi: ok next steps - we'll get you a subset of data and queries, want to see the bench results versus Elastic.
[18:58] Marc: perfect, i'll share the bench script and quickstart.
[19:10] Maya: one final question — do you have a sample contract or pricing ballpark?
[19:15] Lena: yes i'll share hosted pricing sheet and outline Dedicated pricing bands; for now we'll send ballpark estimates and a trial credit.
[19:30] Marc: any other questions?
[19:35] Ravi: none from me, feels like a good next step.
[19:40] Jordan: no, thanks everyone.
[19:45] Lena: great thanks all. recap: Lena send pricing/security + trial; Marc send notebook and bench script; Maya provide 1k dataset + queries; schedule check-in week of 4/6.
[20:05] Marc: thanks, end call.
